differences.what: the tall stack over the 22nd Street flank (T-3799): it stood about 0.55 m off and rose about 1.5 m over the print's, its pots to about y 10 px where the print's stop at y 230. Now at (9.15, 2.25), its cap at 16.65 m and its long pots' lips at about 17.8 m: the shaft within about 15 px (0.3 m) of the print's x 600-690 and the pots' lips within about 10 px of y 230

the round tower at the Prairie/22nd Street corner (T-3800): it stood about 2 m west on the 22nd Street wall, its drum printing about 180 px left of the print's x 625-920. Now set across the corner (K08's round tower across its corner) at the joint fit's axis (13.0, 0.8), its drum prints at about x 613-925 px, within about 12 px of both edges, and the front's first light column, which the build stood at 2.6 m, is gone into the drum as the print shows none between the drum and the canopy

the towers' caps: this print (no earlier than 1905) draws a tall slated spire on each of the three towers and a gabled dormer on the round tower's cap, where the record stands the flat crested caps the Van Osdel print and the 1898 plate show (the declared 1904 state, L-k01-2140-tucker-3770). The phase is argued at the sign-off with the dated pictures (T-3801); until then it stands open

the polygonal tower on the 22nd Street flank: the print draws its axis about x 420 px, about 3 m east of where the build's octagon prints (x about 250), and carries it up a full stage over the main cornice under gabled faces with crockets to its spire

the square tower on the Prairie front's north part (x 1200-1450 px): the print carries it up past the main cornice under its own steep cap, gabled dormer and pinnacles; the build's projection stops under the main mansard and reads as a bay

the gabled dormers and wall gables: the print draws a tall gable over the front's middle light column (x 1010-1150 px), the round tower's gabled dormer and the flank tower's gables, each with crockets and a finial; the build has one street and one flank dormer

the iron fence on its curb with tall stone piers along both streets and the corner pier (x 600-1800 px, y 970-1270): not built (the record's boundary is open; the 20th-22nd block's boundaries are T-3786's)
the arched iron-and-glass canopy over the front walk from the gate to the door (x 1030-1280 px, y 950-1100): not built
the porch and stoop behind the canopy and the fence, and the rear ranges: hidden
the tone of the brick and the stone: the print is monochrome under an overcast sky

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
